Measurement models: the likelihood interface

Source: R/radish_measurement_model.R
terradish_measurement_model.Rd

A measurement model links the graph kernel implied by a conductance surface to the observed genetic response. It is a function of class "terradish_measurement_model" that evaluates a negative log-likelihood, and its derivatives, for a matrix of observed pairwise genetic distances or genetic covariance given a submatrix of the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian. Pass one to the measurement_model argument of terradish.

Details

Choosing a model.

mlpe

Pairwise genetic distances (for example \(F_{ST}\)), with correlation among pairs that share a site. The default.

leastsquares

Pairwise genetic distances with independent errors. Fast; for exploration and diagnostics.

wishart_covariance

An allele-frequency covariance matrix. Requires the effective degrees of freedom nu.

generalized_wishart

Squared distances derived from a covariance matrix. Requires nu and an admissible response (see check_distance_response).

mlpe_covariates, wishart_covariates

Constructors that return a measurement model extended with pairwise environmental covariates (isolation by environment).

Interface. Every measurement model has the signature g(E, S, phi, nu, gradient, hessian, partial, nonnegative, validate). E is the focal-site block of the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian, S is the observed response matrix, phi is the vector of nuisance parameters, and nu is the effective Wishart degrees of freedom (unused by the distance models). Called without phi, the function returns a list with starting values phi and the bounds lower and upper. Called with phi, it returns a list with the negative log-likelihood objective, the expected response fitted, a boundary flag that is TRUE when the resistance coefficient is zero, and, on request, gradient and hessian with respect to phi and the derivative pieces (gradient_E, partial_E, partial_S, jacobian_E, jacobian_S) that terradish uses to differentiate through the graph. The legacy class "radish_measurement_model" is also carried for compatibility.

terradish profiles phi at every value of the conductance parameters, so phi are nuisance parameters. They are reported by summary() on each model's own scale; the same name can mean different things in different models (see the parameter glossary in terradish-package).

Wishart nuisance fitting. For the ordinary two-component wishart_covariance and generalized_wishart models with their standard bounds, nuisance fitting first profiles the overall covariance variance analytically and searches the relative graph/nugget contribution on site contrasts. This deterministic initialization avoids false convergence when a warm log nugget has an almost zero derivative. The existing Newton optimizer then refines the result and computes derivatives at the same parameters. Fixed predictive parameters and custom bounds retain their supplied values and constraints. The finite profile search does not guarantee a global optimum for every possible covariance matrix. A nugget approaching zero remains a limiting estimate and can imply weak nuisance identification.

Worked examples

vignette("v02-wishart-covariance", package = "terradish") for choosing and checking a covariance response, and vignette("v03-mlpe-pairwise-distance", package = "terradish") for pairwise genetic distances.
